title: Deconfounding Actor-Critic Network with Policy Adaptation for Dynamic Treatment Regimes

problem.claim: Individualized ventilation strategies for critically ill patients remain challenging.

gap.claim: Dynamic treatment regime policies learned from electronic health records may be biased by confounders, and long-term-outcome-guided reinforcement learning may penalize effective actions received by non-survivors.

contributions.claim: A deconfounding actor-critic network learns treatment policies using patient resampling and confounding balance modules.
A short-term reward captures immediate health-state changes and is combined with long-term rewards.
A policy adaptation method transfers the learned model to new-source small-scale datasets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On one semi-synthetic and two real-world datasets, the proposed model outperformed state-of-the-art models.
The proposed model provides individualized mechanical-ventilation treatment decisions that could improve patient outcomes.

narrative_sequence.summary: Individualized ventilation for critically ill patients remains difficult, while reinforcement-learning-based dynamic treatment regimes from electronic health records have attracted interest.
Confounders can bias learned policies, and long-term mortality rewards can punish effective actions received by non-survivors.
The study develops a deconfounding actor-critic network with resampling, confounding balance, and short-term rewards combined with long-term rewards.
A policy adaptation method transfers the learned model to new-source small-scale datasets.
The authors report improved performance over state-of-the-art models on one semi-synthetic and two real-world datasets and propose individualized ventilation decisions.

source_observation.claim: Confounding can bias learned treatment policies, while long-term mortality rewards can penalize effective actions received by non-survivors.

interpretation.claim: In observational sequential decision settings, policy learning may need explicit confounding mitigation and rewards sensitive to short-term state changes.

application.claim: Consider combining confounding-balance mechanisms with short-term and long-term reward signals when learning treatment policies from electronic health records.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this combination improves outcomes across other clinical domains or data settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, sample sizes, evaluation metrics, baseline models, or effect magnitudes.
The abstract does not provide details about the confounding assumptions, model architecture, policy adaptation procedure, or treatment-outcome validation.
